card.title: Where am I?
card.blurb: Read your own repository before you change it. Ask git what is waiting to be saved and what you have saved already, then add the next commit knowing exactly where you stand.
hero.title: Where am I?
intro.0: You open a folder on Monday with no memory of how you left it. Did you save that change, or only start it? Git will tell you, but only if you ask - and asking is the habit that separates people who trust git from people who are a bit scared of it. Two questions cover most of it: what is going on right now, and what happened before. Here you learn to ask both, then commit with your eyes open.
task.1.title: Ask before you save
task.1.context:
`git status` answers one question: what is going on in this folder right now. It lists what git is not tracking yet, and what you have staged for the next commit.

The folder holds `dog.txt` and `notes.md`. Only one of them belongs in this save - run `git status` and you will see both waiting.
task.1.goal.0: Run `git status` to see what is waiting.
task.1.goal.1: Stage only `dog.txt` and commit it with `git commit -m "add dog"`.
task.2.title: Read the history you already have
task.2.context:
`git status` looks at now. `git log` looks back - every commit, newest first, each with its message and its **hash**: the short code git uses as that commit's name.

`git log --oneline` is the same list, one commit per line. It is the fastest way to see where you are before you add to it.
task.2.goal.0: Run `git log --oneline` to read the three commits already here.
task.2.goal.1: Then add the next one: stage `feeder.txt` and commit it as `git commit -m "fix the feeder"`.
task.3.title: Where am I? - recap
task.3.context: Two questions, asked before you touch anything.
task.3.summaryIntro: Git never guesses on your behalf, and it never hides what it did. Ask, read the answer, then act - that is the whole habit.
task.3.summaryItems.0.title: `git status` -
task.3.summaryItems.0.text: what is going on right now: what git is not tracking yet, and what you have staged.
task.3.summaryItems.1.title: `git log` -
task.3.summaryItems.1.text: what happened before: every commit, newest first, with its message.
task.3.summaryItems.2.title: `git log --oneline` -
task.3.summaryItems.2.text: the same history, one line each, for when you only need the shape of it.
task.3.summaryItems.3.title: Hash -
task.3.summaryItems.3.text: the short code naming one commit, so you can point at that exact snapshot later.
task.3.summaryClose: Next: branches - how two lines of work grow side by side without touching each other.
